# Understanding the Cairn System

## Pulses and Growth

A pulse causes a cairn to grow taller. The growth has two components: a fixed stride amount plus an additional amount based on how tall the cairn already is. Specifically, you add the stride plus one mark for each complete stride length that fits into the current height. This means taller cairns grow more per pulse than shorter ones.

## Repeated Pulses

When applying multiple pulses in sequence, you must recalculate after each one. The height changes after the first pulse, so the number of complete strides in that new height differs from the original. You cannot pre-calculate using the original height—each pulse operates on the current height at that moment.

## Leaks

A leak removes marks after a pulse occurs. The amount removed depends on the leak value: you lose one mark for every leak-sized group that fits into the newly pulsed height. This is applied to the post-pulse height, not the original height.

## Draining Cycles

A drain cycle combines a pulse followed by mark loss. The drain removes a fixed number of marks regardless of height. Over many cycles, the cairn may stabilize or eventually reach zero if the drain exceeds what the pulse adds.

## Finding Origins

Working backwards from a final height through multiple pulses requires testing candidates by working forward. Since the relationship between starting and ending heights is one-to-one, only one starting height produces any given final height.

## Merging Cairns

Merging combines two cairns using weighted shares (expressed in tenths) and an additional tether value. Each cairn contributes its share-weighted portion (rounded down), and the tether adds an independent component also rounded down. The shares and tether work together—neither alone determines the result.
